---
title: "Total a table by group"
subtitle: "A subtotal closing each block, and a grand total closing the table."
description: "Group rows by a column, label the groups, and close each one with a subtotal before a grand total closes the body."
---

The data carries a column saying which block each row belongs to.
A stub turns one column into row names and that one into groups, then `summary-rows` closes each group and `grand-summary-rows` closes the body.

```typst
#import "@preview/keisen:0.1.0": *

#display-table(
  (
    product: ("Bolt", "Nut", "Beam", "Plate"),
    region: ("North", "North", "South", "South"),
    units: (1250, 860, 430, 2100),
    revenue: (18750.5, 12900.25, 21500, 31500.75),
  ),
  table-header(title: [Regional sales], subtitle: [Financial year 2025 to 2026]),
  table-stub(rowname: "product", group: "region", label: [Product]),
  columns-label(units: [Units], revenue: [Revenue]),
  table-spanner([Performance], ("units", "revenue")),
  format-integer("units"),
  format-number("revenue", decimals: 2),
  summary-rows(functions: (Subtotal: aggregate-sum), columns: ("units", "revenue")),
  grand-summary-rows(functions: (Total: aggregate-sum), columns: ("units", "revenue")),
  table-source-note([Source: internal ledger.]),
  table-options(row-striping: true),
)
```

![A sales table grouped by region, each group closed by a bold subtotal row, with a grand total below and alternate rows shaded.](../assets/examples/grouped.png)

`functions` maps the label the row will carry to the aggregation that fills it, so `(Subtotal: aggregate-sum)` names both at once.
`aggregate-sum` stays in decimal arithmetic, so the totals are exact rather than nearly right.

Striping counts body rows alone, so a group label never takes a stripe or shifts the phase.

Summary rows need groups.
A table with none is closed by `grand-summary-rows` on its own, and rows that no group claims are counted there rather than in a subtotal.
Where the data has no column to group by, [declare the groups in the document](declare-your-own-groups.qmd).
